# controls


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

These constructors return native HTML form controls marked with opt-in
attributes such as `btn` or `input`. The browser manages control state.
Shared CSS applies those states through pseudo-classes (`:disabled`,
`:user-invalid`) and ARIA attributes (`aria-busy`, `aria-pressed`).
Plain FastHTML `Button` and `Input` elements remain unstyled. The Python
constructors emit markup only and include no stylesheets or browser
scripts.

``` python
from fasthtml.common import *
from answerui.demo import demo
from answerui.registry import reg
from fastcore.test import *
from fastlucide.icons import X
```

## Btn

Buttons are raised at rest and sunken while pressed. Pressing shifts the
label, bevels, and shadows without changing outer dimensions. A row of
buttons stays aligned regardless of which ones are pressed.

Three ARIA attributes hold a button in its sunken state without shifting
the label: `aria-busy="true"` for an in-flight request,
`aria-pressed="true"` for a latched toggle, and `aria-expanded="true"`
for an open popover or menu. Each variant controls that appearance
through `--ui-held-face` and `--ui-held-shadow`.

A busy button fades its label and shows a centred spinner without
resizing. Because `aria-busy="true"` changes appearance only, users can
still click a busy button. Set `disabled` to prevent activation.

When a button triggers an htmx request, htmx adds the `htmx-request`
class while the request runs. The busy appearance waits for
`--busy-delay` (default `200ms`) to avoid flashing on fast requests.
Server-set `aria-busy="true"` appears immediately. When a form triggers
the request, htmx adds `htmx-request` to the form instead of the button.
Set `hx-indicator` on the form to target the button.

A disabled button is flat and faded with no shadow while retaining its
variant colour. Re-enabling it restores the raised appearance.

The default `primary` variant uses the accent colour.
`variant='secondary'` uses the neutral surface colour with a hairline
border. `variant='quiet'` has no background, border, or shadow at rest
and inherits the parent text colour. Hovering a quiet button applies
`--tint` (8% alpha). Pressing or holding it applies a 12% tint.

Pass `size='sm'` or `size='lg'` to set `btn-size` for compact or
prominent actions (`None` uses the default size).

Pass `href` to render an `<a>` styled as a button, with the same
variants, sizes, and `icon` option (omitting `type`). Because links have
no native `disabled` state, `:disabled` styling does not apply to them.
Handwritten `<a btn href="...">` elements match the same rules.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Custom variants can override resting padding (`--ui-pad-block`,
`--ui-pad-inline`) or `--relief` without redefining the pressed state.
Below, `compact` tightens padding and `flat` sets `--relief: 0`. Both
variants are registered on `Btn` for this notebook rather than built in.
`doc(Btn)` lists them while they remain registered. To reduce depth
across an entire application, set `:root { --relief: .5; }`.

``` python
Btn.variant('compact', '--ui-pad-block: var(--space-3); --ui-pad-inline: var(--space-2);', doc='Tighter padding.')
Btn.variant('flat', '--relief: 0;', doc='No rims, shadows, or displacement.')
```

    Btn.flat [app] :is([btn])[flat]: No rims, shadows, or displacement.

Flat buttons show their colour states without bevels, shadows, or label

Pass `icon=True` for an icon-only button to make its horizontal padding
match its vertical padding (`--ui-pad-inline: var(--ui-pad-block)`).
Always supply an `aria-label` because an icon has no accessible name.
Buttons containing both an icon and text use standard button padding.

## Text controls

Text controls use inverted bevel lighting (`--bevel-in` and `--sunken`)
to look recessed into the page like a well. Disabled controls flatten to
a muted background without the sunken shadow. `Input`, `Textarea`, and
`Select` add the `input`, `textarea`, and `select` marker attributes.
Handwritten HTML with the same attributes matches the same CSS rules.
`Input` rejects `type='checkbox'`, `type='radio'`, and `type='range'` so
well styling is not applied by mistake; use `Checkbox`, `Radio`, or
`Range` instead, and use FastHTML’s unmarked `Input` for file pickers or
button-type inputs.

Number inputs (`type="number"`) hide browser spin buttons while keeping
keyboard arrow stepping.

Invalid controls show a danger border colour computed from
`--hue-danger`. That rule matches both `:user-invalid` (set by the
browser after interaction) and server-set `aria-invalid="true"`:

## Enabling a button

Render a submit button `disabled` with an `enable` attribute to enable
it automatically when form conditions are met. Set `enable="changed"` to
wait until any control differs from its initial rendered value. Set
`enable="valid"` to wait until the form passes native validation, or
`enable="changed valid"` to require both.

The shared form handler compares each control against its browser
default (`defaultValue`, `defaultChecked`, or `defaultSelected`) without
storing a separate snapshot. Resetting the form disables the button
again. Forms swapped in by htmx work the same way because the browser
treats their rendered values as defaults.

Change the name or enter a valid required email address to enable Save.
Clicking Reset restores the initial values and disables Save again:

``` python
demo(Form(Input(name='name', value='Ada', aria_label='Display name'), Input(name='email', type='email', required=True, placeholder='Email', aria_label='Email'),
    Cluster(Btn('Save', type='submit', disabled=True, enable='changed valid'), Btn('Reset', type='reset', variant='secondary')), stack=True, style='inline-size: 24rem'))
```

``` html
<form enctype="multipart/form-data" stack style="inline-size: 24rem">  <input input name="name" value="Ada" aria-label="Display name">
  <input input name="email" type="email" required placeholder="Email" aria-label="Email">
  <div cluster>
<button type="submit" btn btn-variant="primary" disabled enable="changed valid">Save</button><button type="reset" btn btn-variant="secondary">Reset</button>  </div>
</form>
```

## Group

`Group` wraps related controls in a `div[group]` with shared inner
borders and rounded outer corners. Passing `inset=True` sets
`group-variant="inset"` to render the whole group as a single well with
the action button inside.

`Toolbar` wraps controls in a `div[toolbar][group]` with
`role="toolbar"`. The shared toolbar controller provides a single Tab
stop and moves focus across enabled commands with Left, Right, Home, and
End. Set `aria-pressed` on the server to mark latched toggles. Use
native radios for an exclusive form choice.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Copy

`Copy` renders a `quiet` button (icon-only by default, with
`aria-label="Copy"`) that copies text to the clipboard. Pass `copyfor`
with the `id` of a target element to copy a form control’s `value` or
any other element’s `textContent`. Pass `copy` to copy a fixed string
instead.

For `1.5s` after clicking, the click handler sets the `copied` attribute
on the button and swaps its icon to a check mark. If the button has an
`aria-label`, the handler temporarily sets it to `'Copied'` so screen
readers announce the confirmation. Buttons with visible text labels are
left unchanged. The Clipboard API requires a secure context (HTTPS or
localhost).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Copy

``` python
def Copy(
    *c, copyfor:NoneType=None, copy:NoneType=None, variant:str='quiet', **attrs
):
```

*Copy fixed text or an element’s value or text to the clipboard*

## Click to edit

Use `Btn(..., variant='editable')` for values that are read far more
often than edited. It renders a full-width button with the same padding
and corner radius as a text well, bordered by a dashed hairline (`--n`)
instead of a sunken surface. No input exists until the user clicks.
Visibility does not depend on hover. On click, the application fetches
and swaps in either a single input or a multi-field form. Inside a form,
keep `type="button"` (the default on `Btn`). Set `aria-label` to
describe the edit action because the button’s visible text is the
current value.

The demo below uses a client-only rule to swap each value with its edit
form. Click the name to open an inset input with Save, or click the
schedule to edit day and time. Submitting updates the displayed value.
Pressing Escape or clicking outside cancels and restores the previous
value:

``` python
reg.rule(name='demo-editable', sel='[editable-demo]', on={
    ('& button[btn-variant=editable]', 'click'): r"const p = el.closest('[editable-demo]'); p.firstElementChild.hidden = true; p.lastElementChild.hidden = false; p.querySelector('input, select').focus()",
    ('& form', 'submit'): r"e.preventDefault(); const p = el.closest('[editable-demo]'); p.querySelector('button[btn-variant=editable]').textContent = el.dataset.text.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (_, n) => el.elements[n].value); el.hidden = true; p.firstElementChild.hidden = false",
    ('& form', 'keydown'): r"if (e.key === 'Escape') { el.reset(); el.hidden = true; el.previousElementSibling.hidden = false }",
    (':root', 'pointerdown'): r"for (const f of document.querySelectorAll('[editable-demo] > form:not([hidden])')) if (!f.contains(e.target)) { f.reset(); f.hidden = true; f.previousElementSibling.hidden = false }",
}, doc='Demo only: swaps the value for its form and back in place of the server; a click outside or Escape cancels.')

def _editable_demo(value, form, text, **attrs):
    "An editable value and the hidden form that edits it; `text` is the template that turns the form's fields into the new value"
    return Div(Btn(value, variant='editable', **attrs), Form(form, data_text=text, hidden=True), editable_demo=True)
```

``` python
days = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday']
demo(Stack(
    _editable_demo('Untitled-1', Group(Input(name='name', value='Untitled-1', aria_label='Name'), Btn('Save', type='submit', disabled=True, enable='changed valid'), inset=True),
        '{name}', aria_label='Rename Untitled-1'),
    _editable_demo('Every Monday at 09:00', Group(Select(*[Option(d, selected=d == 'Monday') for d in days], name='day', aria_label='Day'),
        Input(type='time', name='time', value='09:00', aria_label='Time'), Btn('Save', type='submit', disabled=True, enable='changed valid')),
        'Every {day} at {time}', aria_label='Change the schedule'),
    style='inline-size: 24rem'))
```

``` html

<button type="button" btn btn-variant="editable" aria-label="Rename Untitled-1">Untitled-1</button><form enctype="multipart/form-data" data-text="{name}" hidden>      <div group group-variant="inset">
        <input input name="name" value="Untitled-1" aria-label="Name">
<button type="submit" btn btn-variant="primary" disabled enable="changed valid">Save</button>      </div>
</form>  </div>
  <div editable-demo>

<select select name="day" aria-label="Day"><option selected>Monday</option><option>Tuesday</option><option>Wednesday</option><option>Thursday</option><option>Friday</option></select>        <input input type="time" name="time" value="09:00" aria-label="Time">
```

## Switch

submissions. `Switch` returns a native
`<input type="checkbox" role="switch" switch>`, letting the browser

styles the track as a recessed well with a raised thumb that slides
across on `--color-accent` when checked. Inside `Field`, the control
appears before its label just like a checkbox:

## Range

`Range` returns an `<input type="range" range>` styled as a recessed
track with a raised thumb. The shared browser script computes
`--ui-range-fill` from `value`, `min` (default `0`), and `max` (default
`100`) on mount, on `input` or `change`, and after form reset. Scripts
that assign `value` programmatically must dispatch an `input` event to
refresh the track fill.

The shared stylesheet (`03_controls`) defines the WebKit and Firefox
track and thumb rules once. `Range` adds only the `range` attribute.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Field

`Field` pairs a control with its `<label>` plus optional `hint` and
`error` messages so assistive technology announces them together. If the
control lacks an `id`, `Field` generates one and links the `<label>` via
`for`. `Field` sets `field-inline` on switches, checkboxes, and radios
so the control appears before its label text. Because that inline label
uses `justify-self: start`, clicking empty space to the right of the
text does not toggle the control.

`hint` and `error` render as `<small>` elements below the control, with
their ids appended to the control’s `aria-describedby`. Passing `error`
styles the message with `ui-tone="danger"` and sets
`aria-invalid="true"` on the control. Validation rules stay in the
application. `Field` only displays the message you pass.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Field

``` python
def Field(
    label, control, hint:NoneType=None, error:NoneType=None, **attrs
):
```

*A labelled control with optional help and error text*

Native browser validation bubbles appear only on submit and never show
when `enable="valid"` disables the submit button. Instead, the shared
field handler renders the browser’s `validationMessage` inside
`<small validation ui-tone="danger">` under `[field]` when the user
leaves a `:user-invalid` control or when submission fails. On a failed
submit, every invalid field displays its message and the handler focuses
the first invalid control.

While displayed, the validation element’s `id` is added to the control’s
`aria-describedby`. Once the value becomes valid, the handler removes
the `<small validation>` element and strips its `id` from
`aria-describedby`. Server-rendered `error` messages passed to `Field`
have no `validation` attribute and are left untouched by the client
handler.

For form-level server errors, render
`<small validation ui-tone="danger">`
(`Small(msg, ui_tone='danger', validation=True)`) inside the form
outside any `[field]`. Editing any control in the form removes that
form-level message immediately. A `<small validation>` element inside a
`[field]` is cleared only when that field’s control becomes valid.

All control types in one form. The Username field shows both a `hint`
and a server-supplied `error`. Enter an invalid address in Email and
move focus away to trigger client validation:

``` python
Field.demo()
```

Extra keyword arguments (and variants declared on `Field`) are placed on
the outer `div[field]`. Existing attributes on the control remain
intact. Any existing `aria-describedby` ids precede the generated hint
and error ids:

``` python
notes = Textarea(name='notes', aria_describedby='notes-policy')
field = Field('Notes', notes, hint='Keep it brief.', error='Please remove the account number.', compact=True)
assert isinstance(notes.id, str)
test_eq(field.children[0].get('for'), notes.id)
assert notes.attrs['aria-invalid'] == 'true'
assert notes.attrs['aria-describedby'].split() == ['notes-policy', *(o.id for o in field.children[2:])]
test_eq(field.attrs['compact'], True)
notes.attrs
```

    {'textarea': True,
     'name': 'notes',
     'aria-describedby': 'notes-policy _M4PZ8yjWQ9O66BLdN_OPqw _9_mvclUJQKauSCd0wbvWrA',
     'id': '_K1jnDvFmQmqfWxfeu3lObw',
     'aria-invalid': 'true'}

## Fieldset

`Fieldset` renders a native `<fieldset fieldset>` with a hairline border
and inner padding (`--space`) around a `<legend>`. Pass `stack=True` or
another layout attribute to space the fields inside:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Fieldset

``` python
def Fieldset(
    *c, **attrs
):
```

*A bordered group of fields under a legend*

Two checkbox fields under a legend:

``` python
Fieldset.demo()
```

``` html
<fieldset fieldset stack class="gap-2"><legend>Notifications</legend>  <div field field-inline>
<label for="_AYcpoqIuRqKpw2OpUOmAaQ">Email me about mentions</label>    <div field-control>
      <input type="checkbox" checkbox checked id="_AYcpoqIuRqKpw2OpUOmAaQ">
    </div>
  </div>
  <div field field-inline>
<label for="_Yuh6FXDlQDWGmXxxatTRRw">Email me a weekly digest</label>    <div field-control>
      <input type="checkbox" checkbox id="_Yuh6FXDlQDWGmXxxatTRRw">
    </div>
  </div>
</fieldset>
```

To show a field only while a checkbox is checked, set `reveals` on the
checkbox to the target element’s `id`. Match the target’s initial
`hidden` attribute to the checkbox’s initial checked state. On each
`input` or `change` event, the shared handler sets
`target.hidden = !checkbox.checked`:

``` python
demo(Form(Field('Set a monthly limit', Checkbox(name='limit_on', reveals='limit')),
    Field('Monthly limit (US$)', Input(name='limit', type='number', value=200), id='limit', hidden=True), stack=True))
```

``` html
<form enctype="multipart/form-data" stack>  <div field field-inline>
<label for="_hOCerAu8TbmYLmktwWScrQ">Set a monthly limit</label>    <div field-control>
      <input type="checkbox" checkbox name="limit_on" reveals="limit" id="_hOCerAu8TbmYLmktwWScrQ">
    </div>
  </div>
  <div field hidden id="limit">
<label for="_loCEmo5_RDmgQ3SFy6vueg">Monthly limit (US$)</label>    <div field-control>
      <input input name="limit" type="number" value="200" id="_loCEmo5_RDmgQ3SFy6vueg">
    </div>
  </div>
</form>
```
